h1: Loral hops for floral lagers and gentle pale ales
title: Loral Hops for Floral Lagers | Craft Beer School
desc: How to use Loral hops in a floral lager or gentle pale ale: dry hop and whirlpool rates in g/hl for a 10 hl brewhouse and the oxygen traps to avoid.
teaser: Loral smells of flowers and lemon peel, with a faint peppery edge. It is built for beers that do not shout.
standfirst: Loral is a modern American hop that gives floral and herbal lift without fruit-bomb weight. This guide shows professional brewers how to dose it in lagers and pale ales and how to protect a delicate aroma.
sections: A floral hop for restrained beers

Loral is a newer American variety from the Hop Breeding Company. Brewers describe it as floral and herbal, with lemon peel and a touch of black pepper. Supplier sheets put its alpha acid in the low double digits, so it can carry bitterness as well. Always use the figure on the analysis for your lot.

Its appeal is balance. It does not push tropical fruit or resin, so it suits beers where malt and yeast should still lead: pilsner, helles, a pale ale at 4.5% ABV or an English style bitter with a modern finish.

For a 10 hl brewpub batch of pilsner or helles, a restrained late hop is usually enough. A starting point:

  • Whirlpool at about 80 °C for 20 minutes: 30 to 50 g per hl, so 300 to 500 g.
  • Cold side hop (Kaltgehopft) at fermentation end, 10 to 12 °C, 20 to 40 g per hl for two to three days.

Cold dry hopping a lager gives a bright, floral top note that a kettle addition cannot match. It also needs care with oxygen, which we come to below.
Dosing in a gentle pale ale

A pale ale at 4.5% ABV and 25 to 30 IBU asks for more. Try 100 to 200 g per hl in the dry hop, split into two additions if your fermenter allows: the first near the end of active fermentation, the second after the yeast has been dumped. Whirlpool at 75 to 80 °C adds depth with little extra bitterness, though count what it adds.

Because the character is floral and herbal, Loral pairs well with a pale base. Our guide to Weyermann extra pale premium pilsner malt covers a base that keeps the grist clean. For a fruitier partner, see Amarillo and Palisade.

Delicate hop aroma is the first thing oxygen takes. A dry hop addition through an open manway lets air in. Hop pellets carry some in as well. Dissolved oxygen in packaged beer should stay as low as your equipment allows. In practice that means purging the hop dosing port with CO2, adding the hops under a positive gas blanket and keeping transfers closed.

If your plant has no hop dosing vessel, a purged stainless bucket with a sanitary connection is a modest fix. Measure dissolved oxygen after the transfer to bright tank and again at packaging. Compare the two. The numbers tell you where oxygen is getting in.
Floor detail: the dry hop and the cold chain

Dry hop lagers need a cold tank with a working glycol jacket. In summer a chiller shared across many tanks can run out of capacity when several tanks crash at once. Schedule the cold dry hop for a day when the chiller is not also crash cooling two ales. If the temperature climbs above 14 °C during the contact, you will pull more grassy notes and risk hop creep from residual enzymes if yeast is still active.

American hops arrive as T90 pellets in nitrogen flushed foil. Check the crop year on the pack and ask the importer how the lot was stored. A floral hop loses its character faster than a bittering variety. Store at or below 0 °C. For a late hop, open a fresh pack and use all of it where possible.

Buy a small amount for a trial before you commit a season. Change nothing else in the recipe, brew twice with different dry hop rates and compare in a blind tasting with your team, with spit cups for anyone who wants them.
Why it is worth learning properly

Keep a simple trial log for every hop lot: alpha, crop year, dose, temperature and contact time, with a tasting score. After four or five trials you will know what Loral does in your own beer and water rather than relying on a spec sheet.

A floral lager hop is easy to under-dose and easy to spoil. It rewards a brewer who understands how oils behave through whirlpool, fermentation and packaging. That chain of cause and effect is where hop work moves from recipe copying to design.
faqs: Floral and herbal, with lemon peel and a little black pepper. It is less fruity and less resinous than most modern American varieties.
Can Loral be used in lagers?
Yes. A whirlpool at about 80 °C and a short cold dry hop give a bright floral note without turning the beer into an ale.
How much Loral should I dry hop with?
For a gentle pale ale, 100 to 200 g per hl is a reasonable range. For a lager, start at 20 to 40 g per hl.
Why does my dry hopped lager lose aroma so quickly?
Oxygen is the usual cause. Purge the hop dosing port, keep transfers closed and check dissolved oxygen at each step.
